overall_assessment: Anonymization works well for nord. None of the 28 courses, and none of the 176 pilot offerings in a separate scan, has a name, e-mail or phone number left: nord pages have no contact block, and 'emneansvarlig' and 'faglærer' occur only as roles. All 8 name_like flags are false alarms on reference authors (McKenzie, Taleb), organisations (Det Norske Teatret, Kedge Business School), products (Power BI, Adobe Premiere) and states. The removals are correct and leave readable text (the COVID notes' 'Våren 2021:' and 'våren 2020', 'Spring 2026:', clock times, a dated deadline). The regulation date '28.10.2020 nr. 2474' is now kept, and the earlier 'MERK: :' artifact is gone. Three rare, low-severity issues remain, each in one or two of the 3644 nord rows: (1) the semester-label rule cuts 'høst'/'vår' from course names that end in 'Skoleeksamen'; (2) one PhD course keeps a misspelt 'Sprign 2026:' label; (3) the same course keeps the dates of its weekday timetable.

findings.evidence: finansregnskap med analyse - Skoleeksamen [−høst−] - 5 Studiepoeng … finansregnskap med analyse - Skoleeksamen [−vår−] - 5 Studiepoeng
findings.description: The rule that removes a season word after a semester label also removes yearless season words that are part of course names. In the credit-overlap list, 'BE101E-004 … - Skoleeksamen høst' and 'BE101E-005 … - Skoleeksamen vår' both become '… - Skoleeksamen', so the two overlapping courses can no longer be told apart. The rubric keeps course names, and keeps season words that are not semester labels; the spec keeps credit overlap in course_plan. Outside the packet, the same rule damages prose. In nord_LED5018-1_2022_autumn_2, 'med oppstart høst. Det åpnes' becomes 'med oppstart Det åpnes': the sentence's full stop goes with the season word and two sentences run together. The season word could go as a 'teaching start' under the spec, but the full stop should stay. In all 3644 nord rows the rule removes a yearless season word in 7 rows. Five of them are 'Praktisk eksamen' followed by 'Vårsemesteret.', an assessment-semester label that the spec leaves out, so that removal is correct. The other two are these cases.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: This is the 'after a semester label' str_remove_all in .anon_generic() (R/anonymize.R). Its lookbehind (?<=(?i:semester|undervisning|oppstart|startsemester|eksamen)[:\s]{0,3}) does not require the label to start a word. It therefore fires on the end of compounds such as 'Skoleeksamen' and 'hjemmeeksamen'. The trailing [.,]?[ \t]* also consumes a full stop that ends a sentence in the middle of a line.
findings.suggested_fix:
In that rule, (1) match the label as a word of its own and list the compounds that should still match. One way is to turn it into str_replace_all(..., "\1") with the capture group ((?<!\p{L})(?i:(?:undervisnings|eksamens|start)?semester|undervisning|oppstart|eksamen)[:\s]{0,3}) in front of the season pattern. 'Skoleeksamen høst' then no longer matches. (2) Replace [.,]? with (?:,|\.(?=[ 	]*(?:
|$)))? so that a full stop in the middle of a line stays. Add tests to tests/testthat/test-anonymize.R: 'BE101E-004 - Driftsregnskap og finansregnskap med analyse - Skoleeksamen høst - 5 Studiepoeng' stays unchanged; 'med oppstart høst. Det åpnes' keeps its full stop; 'Undervisningssemester: Vår' and 'Praktisk eksamen

Vårsemesteret.' are still removed.

findings.description: A semester label with a year is left because the source misspells 'Spring'. The same block's correctly spelled 'Spring 2026:' (after 'Teaching') is removed, but the plan is still dated to spring 2026 by this label. The rubric removes semester labels with a year. In all 3644 nord rows, this is the only row with the problem.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: .season_regex in R/anonymize.R matches only correctly spelled season words. The year rules in .anon_generic() remove a bare year only next to admin keywords (opprettet, godkjent, gyldig fra, …), and 'Assessment' is not one of them.
findings.suggested_fix: Either accept it as a one-off typo in the source, or add a typo-tolerant rule to .anon_generic() that catches a year label closing a line after an assessment or teaching heading, whatever its season word: str_replace_all("(?m)^((?i:assessment|teaching|vurdering|undervisning|eksamen)\\b)[ \\t]+\\p{L}+[ \\t]+20\\d{2}:[ \\t]*$", "\\1"), wrapped in .not_gov_rule. Test: 'Assessment Sprign 2026:' -> 'Assessment'.

findings.description: A teaching timetable keeps its session dates: 'Week 11, Thursday 12.3', 'Week 13, Friday 27.3', 'Week 16, Thursday 16.4', 'Week 19, Thursday 7.5.'. The block's clock times ('11:00 – 15:00') and its dated deadline ('11.6.2026 14:00') were removed, but day.month dates without a year are not matched. The spec leaves timetables (weeks, lecture times, exam dates, deadlines) and administrative dates out of course_plan. Together with the weekdays, these dates place the plan in 2026. In all 3644 nord rows, this is the only row with the problem. Yearless recurring application deadlines elsewhere ('senest 20. januar', 'innen 15. mai') do not date the plan and are fine.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: The date rules in .anon_generic() (R/anonymize.R) require a year (dd.mm.yyyy, zero-padded dd.mm.yy, long dates with a year). A bare 'd.m' is left alone on purpose, because it cannot be told apart from credits ('7.5'), decimals and section numbers.
findings.suggested_fix: In .anon_generic(), remove a day.month date only when a weekday comes right before it, which never happens with credits or section numbers: str_replace_all("((?i:(?:mon|tues|wednes|thurs|fri|satur|sun)day|(?:man|tirs|ons|tors|fre|lør|søn)dag)),?[ \\t]+\\d{1,2}\\.\\d{1,2}\\.?(?![\\d.])", "\\1"). Test: 'Week 13, Friday 27.3' -> 'Week 13, Friday'; 'Studiepoeng 7.5' stays unchanged.
